Thanks Connor — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from FinSecure's security team: 

- Time window: we need the last 30 days first; we may request older history if the data looks right.
- Identity: we need an auditable principal column that maps to our internal user_id. Including the original user email is ok only if it is one-way hashed (SHA256) and accompanied by the salt/hash metadata so we can reproduce.
- Required columns: timestamp (ISO8601), principal_id (string), principal_type (user/service), action (read/write/infer), resource (full path), request_id, session_id, source_ip, model_version, response_token_count.
- Export format: CSV is preferred as our compliance tools ingest CSV; JSONL acceptable. Parquet not required for now.
- Retention & deletion evidence: we require documentation showing retention policy (24 months), automated deletion/archival processes, and a sample deletion audit log proving removal of data for a test object.

Can you also confirm: are exports generated from the hosted API logs or from a separate export pipeline (S3 manifest)? We need the provenance for our audit.

Looping in our security engineer, Luke Chen (luke.chen@finsecure.com), who will review the sample. Please send the sample as an S3 presigned link or secure Drive link. We need the sample within 7 calendar days for our procurement timeline.

Elena
Director, Information Security

Hi all — thanks for the clear ask, Elena. I've prepared a sample export and a short explanation of how we produce and secure these artifacts. Attached: access-history-sample-20260630.csv, redwood-export-manifest-20260630.json, redwood-pseudonymization-options.pdf (attachment stubs).

Quick notes on the CSV sample (attached):
- Columns included: iso_timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_path, request_id, session_id, source_ip, model_version, response_token_count, raw_email_hash
- raw_email_hash is SHA256(email + per-export salt). The manifest contains the salt identifier and hashing algorithm used so you can verify. We do NOT include unhashed email in hosted exports unless customer explicitly requests and signs an exception.
- Provenance: the export was produced from our ingestion/backplane export pipeline (export job id: EJ-20260630-88). The manifest includes S3 object keys and SHA256 checksums for each file; we can provide a presigned S3 link for download.
- Export formats we support: CSV, JSONL, Parquet. Delivery: S3 presigned or secure Drive.
- Retention: default retention for hosted customers is 90 days. For Dedicated or Private deployments we support configurable retention up to 24 months; this requires a retention clause in the contract and a configuration change in the tenant config. Laura can advise on contract language.
- Proof-of-deletion: we generate deletion_event logs (audit entries) when data is purged; those are retained for an additional 30 days beyond data retention and are included in the deletion audit bundle (manifest + signed checksum). We can provide a redacted deletion event proving a test object was removed on request.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will produce a 30-day sample filtered to the time window Elena confirms (we used 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30 in the attached sample).
2) I will package the manifest and provide the presigned link.
3) Connor / Laura will confirm whether FinSecure needs contract language for 24-month retention and any EU residency commitments.

Deliverable ETA: preliminary sample and manifest by Fri 2026-07-03 17:00 PDT (48 hours from now). If FinSecure needs the 7-day calendar SLA, we'll still meet it.
